title: POC Weekly Sync: Quantization (INT8/FP8)
next_steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark spreadsheet with INT8/FP8 runs and confidence intervals
Customer to provide 2 additional eval prompt sets by 2025-08-19
Schedule infra deep-dive for VPC setup with Mark next week
action_items: Alex Chen: upload combined perf/quality sheet to shared drive by 2025-08-14
Priya Singh: send two additional eval prompt sets (conversational + instructions) by 2025-08-19
Sara Patel: prepare config diff for INT8 vs FP8 rollout and include quantization knobs by 2025-08-15
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quantization experiment results. INT8 shows ~1.7-1.9x throughput improvements with small quality regressions on edge prompts; FP8 gives milder perf gains (~1.3-1.5x) with lower quality impact. Next steps are to run larger eval sets, tune per-layer scales, and plan a canary on Dedicated capacity.
topics: deployment plan: dedicated vs hosted canary
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-12 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Sara Patel (Redwood SE), John Rivera (Acme CTO), Priya Singh (Acme ML Engineer), Mark Li (Acme Infra)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync on quantization, um, we'll run about 45 minutes, we have results to show and some tuning suggestions. Sara and I will go first then open for questions.
[00:18] John Rivera: great, thanks Alex. quick note, Priya's got a calendar conflict at 15:30 so she might drop for last 10 min.
[00:25] Sara Patel: cool, I'll start with a quick recap of the experiment matrix — we ran the same model family you provided (oak-7b-ish, note transcripts call it "oak" sometimes), baseline fp16, int8 with per-channel symmetric, and an fp8 prototype mode (experimental kernel).
[00:43] Priya Singh: can you remind us which infra these ran on? we care about the GPU type for throughput numbers.
[00:50] Sara Patel: yes — everything here was on g5.4x instances (A100-style — actually it's A10x, sorry transcription mislabels), on Redwood Dedicated pool. for the canary we also did a small hosted run on an nvidia t4 equivalent.
[01:10] Mark Li: ok. one thing — for the dedicated numbers, was KV cache enabled? our live workloads are heavy prefix reuse.
[01:16] Sara Patel: good call, yes KV cache was enabled for the main bench runs; we also have a no-cache run in appendix. the main throughput deltas include the cache benefit.
[01:28] Alex Chen: i'll share the high-level delta — feel free to stop and ask if anything's confusing. INT8 reduced per-token latency and increased throughput by roughly 1.7x to 1.9x depending on sequence length and batch. FP8 gave 1.3x to 1.5x improvements but with better numerical stability in some layers.
[01:46] John Rivera: that's promising. how about quality — we need to know if generation accuracy or instruction-following drops.
[01:52] Sara Patel: we ran three eval sets: conversational, instruction-writing, and domain-specific robotics prompts. aggregate QA accuracy (we use exact-match-ish + human spot checks) dropped by ~1.2-2.5% on INT8 on the hardest prompt set, FP8 showed ~0.4-1.0% drop. specific edge cases — long context chain-of-thought and numeric extraction — showed bigger deltas under INT8.
[02:18] Priya Singh: hmm, that aligns with what we feared. are those numbers statistically significant? sample sizes?
[02:25] Sara Patel: current runs are O(5k) prompts per set; CI is tight enough to be meaningful but we want your extra evals for the domain prompts. see the spreadsheet we shared — link in the notes: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-quant-aug2025 (placeholder link).
[02:40] John Rivera: i see. do you have examples of failure modes? can we get diffs?
[02:45] Sara Patel: yes — we included a short regression set in the doc. examples: hallucinated actuator command id, truncated bracketed sequences, and a few instruction-miss cases where the model omitted a required safety guard. many of those are low frequency but high-impact for you.
[03:05] Mark Li: safety guard omission — that's a dealbreaker for production unless we can mitigate. what mitigation approaches do you recommend?
[03:12] Alex Chen: quick list — 1) per-layer mixed precision (keep attention/FFN in fp16 for critical layers), 2) targeted fallback: run safety-critical prompts on fp16 or FP8-only, 3) post-filtering/heuristic checks for certain output patterns, 4) distillation or small fine-tune for robustness.
[03:33] Priya Singh: i like the targeted fallback idea — so route those prompts to baseline. how heavy is the routing complexity?
[03:39] Sara Patel: Redwood runtime supports policy routing today — you can tag routes by prompt type or caller. the config we prototype is route.rules -> if prompt contains safety-token or length > X, then use fp16; otherwise INT8. we can share an example config.
[03:54] John Rivera: performance numbers with mixed precision — any middle ground?
[03:58] Sara Patel: yes, mixed precision where we keep attention weights in fp16 and quantize FFN to int8 gives ~1.4x throughput and negligible quality regression for most prompts. it's a good compromise.
[04:12] Alex Chen: we also experimented with per-channel scales and calibration methods (min-max vs MSE vs KL based). the best INT8 runs used KL-scaling per-channel with a small calibration set, that reduced worst-case regressions.
[04:26] Priya Singh: what's the compute overhead for calibration?
[04:29] Sara Patel: calibration is cheap — a few hundred samples once per model variant, seconds to minutes depending on infra. it's a one-time step for a quantized model build.
[04:40] John Rivera: ok. curious about FP8 — we saw better numeric stability in some tests, why not just use FP8 everywhere?
[04:47] Sara Patel: FP8 is promising — lower perf gain than INT8 but better fidelity; however kernel support is still experimental in some runtimes and quantized format interoperability with KV cache across model versions needs more validation. also some vendor drivers have quirks, so we treat FP8 as a near-term option with more guarded rollout.
[05:08] Mark Li: driver quirks are our nightmare. do you track which GPUs had issues? we plan to run on multiple clouds.
[05:15] Sara Patel: yes — we have a matrix. on Ampere A100-ish kernel we saw consistent FP8 behavior, on older T4-equivalents it was flaky; we'll share the compatibility table in the sheet.
[05:28] John Rivera: can we talk SLOs — if we move to INT8 can Redwood guarantee latency windows for our 95th pct?
[05:35] Alex Chen: we can set SLO targets on Dedicated with reserved capacity. our Dedicated offering supports SLO-backed latency targets; for canary we suggest a small dedicated pool to validate 95p under production traffic. also caching/batching policies affect 95p; our recommendations are in the console config.
[05:52] Priya Singh: any cost delta estimates? we want unit economics.
[05:56] Sara Patel: rough ballpark — INT8 reduces per-token GPU cost by 30-45% due to higher throughput; FP8 is ~20-30%. exact numbers depend on host type and KV cache hit rate. we'll put cost sheets per-instance in the benchmark doc.
[06:12] John Rivera: good. how about rollout plan — steps to go from test to canary?
[06:16] Alex Chen: proposed plan: 1) expanded evals with your extra prompt sets (this week), 2) calibration runs and mixed-precision config (by 2025-08-15), 3) canary on small Dedicated pool for 1 week with close monitoring and regression alarms (target start 2025-08-19), 4) increment traffic if metrics hold.
[06:36] Priya Singh: timeline sounds ok. i want to see alerting tied to quality regressions not just latency. can Redwood hook eval degradation to our alerting?
[06:44] Sara Patel: yes — Redwood Optimize can run continuous quality monitors and fire regression alerts when a prompt set's metric degrades beyond threshold; we can push alerts to your pager or Slack integration.
[06:54] Mark Li: on the infra side, we'll need a VPC peering step and KMS key exchange for encryption. any templates?
[07:01] Alex Chen: we have a VPC onboarding checklist and KMS integration doc — will share link. also for Private deployment we can do a full on-prem package if needed but for now Dedicated with VPC peering should be fine.
[07:12] John Rivera: can you spell out the rollback plan if we see regressions in canary?
[07:15] Sara Patel: simple — auto-fallback policy: if quality alert or latency > threshold, route traffic back to fp16 variant and scale down quantized instances; we can also have a gradual decremental rollout.
[07:29] Priya Singh: technical Q: you mentioned per-layer quantization knobs — can we choose layer ranges to keep FP16 manually?
[07:35] Sara Patel: yes — our quantization builder supports a layer include/exclude list and per-layer scale override. we typically exclude first N attention layers or last FFN if those are sensitive.
[07:47] Alex Chen: i'll pause — any other questions?
[07:50] John Rivera: quick one — sample logs for regression detection, will you provide diffs and example traces?
[07:55] Sara Patel: yes, we have sample request/response pairs and a regression log that shows token-level differences; we'll attach to the sheet.
[08:04] Priya Singh: okay i'm going to drop in a few minutes but thanks this is actionable.
[08:08] Alex Chen: thanks Priya. next steps recap — Alex to upload combined perf/quality sheet; Priya to send more evals; Sara to prepare config diff. any objections to the 2025-08-19 canary start?
[08:24] John Rivera: works for us pending the extra eval runs.
[08:28] Mark Li: same.
[08:30] Alex Chen: great. i'll follow up in email with links and calendar invite for infra deep-dive. thanks everyone.
[08:35] [END]
